answer: In an agent market, the bridge from identity to voting power is a token deposit locked for 90 days: votes count by deposited value, never by account count. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents still buys only 100 tokens of influence. Viewed through this prism, a tide of fake identities gains nothing by multiplying names. To gain control, an attacker must acquire and lock enough real stake, paying its purchase price and losing access to that capital during the lock.
